findings.summary: The "three encodings, without a BOM" gate does not assert that Console.InputEncoding has an empty preamble.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261126-1034-b43-i162-pwsh-gates-utf8.loop-brief.md:66 requires all three encodings to be UTF-8 without a BOM, but the literal gate at lines 133-134 checks InputEncoding.CodePage only. Its preamble checks cover OutputEncoding and $OutputEncoding, so InputEncoding could be a BOM-emitting UTF-8 encoding and the gate would still exit 0.
findings.fix: Add `-or [Console]::InputEncoding.GetPreamble().Length -ne 0` to the pinned condition at line 134.

decisions: vloop sets UTF-8 inside the pwsh/powershell process on every OS rather than relying only on documentation or changing global machine/profile state; this is sound for the stated goal.
Console.OutputEncoding, Console.InputEncoding and $OutputEncoding all use BOM-less UTF-8; this is sound, subject to the gate correction above.
The implementer may choose the PowerShell setup mechanism; leaving this open is sound because the observable contract is exact.
The test fixture is the literal `café`, with the stdin hash computed from the platform line ending; this is sound.
The guide recommends only `[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()` for a person's terminal pipeline; this matches the documented symptom.
